confidentUnsupported.evidence: 'even if the external hook looks fine, the internal latch may be broken or misaligned so the machine no longer detects a closed door... I recommend you remove the duvet and call an engineer to fit a new door catch assembly'

unjustifiedPart.evidence: 'call an engineer to fit a new door catch assembly'

rationale: The assistant misread the opener ('wont start', door shut) as a door-stuck-locked problem, then framed the duvet as an 'unbalanced load' fault, only reaching the correct overload explanation after the customer volunteered that the duvet was bulging and squashed in the seal. It never asked the key check (does it start with a normal load) and, when the customer asked 'is it just too much duvet', it hedged and then asserted the internal latch was likely snapped despite the customer reporting the hook looked fine. It ended by recommending an engineer and a new door catch assembly for what the evidence shows is simply an overfilled drum with no fault, plus a parts-shopping model-number panel, so a UK homeowner would face an unnecessary callout and part cost.
